framework: Five-dimension quality framework grounded in Batini et al. (2009) and Wang & Strong (1996). Thresholds pre-registered in config/thresholds.yaml (signed off: Dr. Tobias Cibis, 2026-09-09).
determinism_note: All source reports are deterministic. This report is therefore fully deterministic. No timestamps are included.

intentional_removals.description: E4 TEMP warm-up artefact samples set to NaN during cleaning. Documented in reports/wesad_cleaning.json. Excluded from missingness_rate by definition (intentional, not unintended absence).

completeness.completeness_definition_note: Missingness measures UNINTENDED absence only. Samples intentionally removed during cleaning are excluded from the rate and reported separately. Decision: Kevin, 2026-10-12.

before.violation_cause: E4 TEMP warm-up artefact: all 60 violations were indices 0-3 of the TEMP channel (~382 degrees C) across all 15 participants. All other signals: zero violations.

validity_conformance.headline: Conformance violations: 60 (Bronze) -> 0 (Gold). Pipeline resolved the only conformance issue in the dataset.

before.violation_cause: Same 60 TEMP warm-up samples as the conformance violations. Physiologically implausible (~382 degrees C, above the 42 degrees C skin-temperature ceiling). Zero device-flagged violations.

validity_plausibility.headline: Plausibility failures: 60 (Bronze) -> 0 (Gold). The only physiologically implausible signal was the TEMP warm-up artefact, resolved by cleaning.

before.interpretation: The ~19-minute gap is a sensor activation-window difference: the E4 wristband activates ~15-24 minutes before the RespiBAN chest sensor. This is resolved by trimming to the shared overlap window. It is NOT a residual the threshold measures.
before.note: Threshold does not apply to the raw start-time gap.

after.note: 12/15 participants: zero residual. S2/S3/S4: residuals up to 0.107 s, within the E4 EDA quantisation bound of +/-0.125 s. All 15 participants pass the 1.0 s threshold.

timeliness.limitation: Partly assessed. The 5-point reconstruction method verifies internal consistency within the overlap window but cannot detect a uniform start-time shift applied to both devices simultaneously. Fault injection confirmed that shifts of 0.5 s to 3600 s all went undetected.

consistency.recorded_decision: No dedicated consistency metric defined for WESAD. Documented in config/thresholds.yaml (consistency block) and docs/progress_log.md. The systematic ~19-minute timing mismatch between E4 and RespiBAN sensors is a timeliness/alignment matter measured under max_cross_modal_offset_seconds; treating it as consistency as well would double-count the same phenomenon. To be revisited for DEAP (Task 14).

accuracy.stated_limitation: No accuracy metric is defined. Accuracy in the sense of 'ground-truth agreement' requires an external reference standard (e.g. a calibrated lab instrument or simultaneous clinical measurement). No such reference is available for WESAD. This is a known limitation of the framework for this dataset, recorded deliberately rather than silently omitted. Absent an accuracy metric, the framework cannot assess whether the physiological values themselves are correct, only that they are complete, conformant, within plausible bounds, and temporally aligned. See config/thresholds.yaml (accuracy is intentionally absent).

overall_assessment.headline: The Gold pipeline resolves the only quality issues found in WESAD. Conformance and plausibility violations fall from 60 to 0 after cleaning the E4 TEMP warm-up artefact. Completeness after cleaning: unintentional missingness = 0.0 (60 intentional removals reported separately). Cross-modal alignment passes the 1.0 s threshold (max residual 0.107 s; timeliness partly assessed: the check cannot detect uniform start-time shifts). All four measured dimensions pass. The framework demonstrates end-to-end detection, documentation, and resolution of a real quality issue.
